newsitem.title: USA: J.C. Penney Q1 store operating profit down.
newsitem.headline: J.C. Penney Q1 store operating profit down.

text.p: J.C. Penney Co Inc said on Tuesday that the first-quarter operating profit for its J.C. Penney stores and catalog was down $10 million from the same period the year before, a decline the company attributed to a slight decline in the gross margin ratio and a slight increase in the operating expense ration.

At the end of the quarter, stores and catalog inventory levels were above plan, but the company said it has taken steps to bring its inventory in line with expected sales volume over the next few months.
The company reported first quarter net income per share of $0.53, compared to $0.57 for the first quarter of 1996, on a fully diluted basis.

But J.C. Penney said its overall operating profit before interest, amortization, business acquisition expenses and taxes was $352 million for the first quarter of 1997, up 40 percent from last year's first quarter.
This year's results included charges totaling $43 million from drugstore acquisitions.
J.C. Penney said its Eckerd drugstores operating profit was $128 million, up 30 percent from the 1996 period on a pro forma basis. Operating profit margin improved 80 basis points, the company said.

Among the steps the company said it has taken to improve its position were issuing $3 billion in debt to fund the Eckerd acquisition and lower the average cost of its long-term debt; and launching a new "J.C. Penney -- I Love your style" marketing campaign.
